models_evaluated: simulated AI diagnostic aid for intracranial hemorrhage and large-vessel occlusion

links.outcome: Reader accuracy with versus without AI aid, and reliance on incorrect AI results, by trainee level
links.effect: Medical student accuracy improved 11.0 points (P<.001) with aid; residents no significant change. Both groups considerably less accurate when disagreeing with or given incorrect AI results; students less accurate than AI alone.
links.quote: Both groups were considerably less accurate when disagreeing with the artificial intelligence or when supplied with an incorrect artificial intelligence result.

links.outcome: Whether trainees detected and overruled incorrect AI outputs
links.effect: Both groups considerably less accurate with incorrect AI results; medical students less likely than residents to overrule incorrect AI interpretations and less accurate with aid than AI alone.
links.quote: However, medical students were less likely than resident trainees to overrule incorrect artificial intelligence interpretations and were less accurate, even with diagnostic aid, than the artificial intelligence was by itself.

screen.reason: Evaluates the impact of AI diagnostic assistance on trainee accuracy and overreliance/automation bias across different experience levels (medical students vs. residents).

primary.practice: AI-assisted clinician interpretation across experience levels
